01.r: Every part of the tithe of animals.
01.n: The KJV's 'concerning' makes the phrase a heading, which is how it works: it names the subject before the rule.

02.r: The tenth owed to God, now of livestock.
02.n: The same noun as for the tithe of the land two verses earlier. Our register renders it 'tithe' throughout.

03.n: Gesenius: an ox, whether bull or cow, so called from its ploughing. BDB: cattle, herd, mostly collective. There is no article in the Hebrew.

04.r: The smaller livestock: sheep and goats.
04.n: Gesenius: a collective noun, flocks, small cattle, that is, sheep and goats, and set against the word for herds. The DRC spells it out as 'sheep, and goats'.

05.r: Each animal, counted one by one.
05.n: Here the word stands alone: 'all, everything'. It restates the subject before the rule is given.

06.r: Introduces the animals that pass under the rod.

07.r: Each animal walks past in turn.
07.n: Gesenius gives the root sense TO PASS OVER. The verb is imperfect, describing what happens each time.

08.r: Beneath the staff held out over the animals.

09.r: The shepherd's staff held over the animals as they pass.
09.n: Gesenius: a staff, stick, rod; BDB also lists the sense 'tribe' for this word. That the rod was held out to count the animals one by one is a reasonable reading; the Greek translators add 'in the count'. The DRC and BSB add 'shepherd's'.

10.n: An ordinal number, 'the tenth', a different word from the noun 'tithe' at the head of the verse. Gesenius: tenth.

11.r: States the rule for the tenth animal.

12.r: Set apart for God, not for common use.
12.n: A noun, 'holiness' or 'a holy thing', not an adjective; Gesenius gives first 'holiness'. The DRC says 'sanctified'.

13.r: Holy as belonging to the LORD.

_extra.9: ἐν (in): begins a phrase added in the Greek, 'in the count'.
_extra.10: τῷ (the): part of the added phrase.
_extra.11: ἀριθμῷ (count, number): the Greek adds 'in the count', 'whatever comes in the count under the rod'.

04.n: The word printed αἰ in our Greek text is evidently καὶ cut short. The Greek word for sheep that the sense calls for after it is missing from our text; most likely the digital copy dropped it.

07.n: ὃ ἐὰν ἔλθῃ, 'whatever comes': the Greek has 'come' for 'pass'.
